episode_title: How Winsupply Runs M&A With Just Four People

real_qa.q: How does Winsupply structure its M&A team and what makes its deal performance exceed industry standards?
real_qa.r: Winsupply runs M&A with just four core people: Greg Holbrook (negotiations), Steve Cohen (operational diligence), Stacy (project manager), and Claire (financial analyst). Over 80% of Winsupply deals meet or beat expectations, driven by focusing on people alignment, understanding the business deeply through diligence, and maintaining local autonomy post-acquisition. The success comes from having like-minded individuals supported by consistent external vendor partners like Brixie Meyer for quality of earnings and Seablee Shilton Dyers for legal work.
real_qa.requete: Winsupply M&A team structure deal success rate

real_qa.q: Why does Winsupply not operate as a traditional roll-up despite acquiring over 20 companies?
real_qa.r: Winsupply is a collective of over 680 local companies that operates through a support service campus rather than a traditional roll-up. The company integrates acquisitions at what Greg calls 'local speed,' prioritizing least disruption to customers and employees. Winsupply maintains 51% ownership in local companies while allowing employees and management to own equity, make local pricing and vendor decisions, and operate under previous DBAs. This approach keeps founders energized and sellers stay longer than initially planned because they retain autonomy and can still build relationships with customers.
real_qa.requete: Winsupply roll-up model local autonomy acquisition strategy

real_qa.q: What is Winsupply's approach to ERP integration timing for newly acquired companies?
real_qa.r: Winsupply converts acquired companies to its WISE ERP system only when conditions allow for safe transition—not on a forced timeline. During the CAR Supply integration (22 locations in Ohio and Michigan from 2013, completed in November 2021), Winsupply split each location into separate C-Corps at conversion time to provide ownership structure to employees. The company prioritizes not disrupting the customer base and ensures reliable data before migration. Greg states: 'Our ERP is a great tool, but what we don't want to do is disrupt the customer base. At the end of the day, we're all here to service the customer.'
real_qa.requete: Winsupply ERP integration WISE system acquisition timing

real_qa.q: How has Winsupply's diligence process evolved from checklist-based to relationship-driven?
real_qa.r: Early in Winsupply's formalized M&A process, diligence was checklist-driven with box-checking and incomplete evaluation. Greg evolved the approach to be relationship-focused by coaching sellers through each information request, explaining why data is needed, and ensuring transparency. Rather than asking sellers to create documents, Winsupply works with existing materials. Greg personally writes legal language with sellers and negotiates directly without routing through intermediaries, cutting red tape and enabling faster deal completion. This shift emphasizes communication mechanisms and mutual benefit over procedural hurdles.
real_qa.requete: diligence process seller communication trust building M&A

real_qa.q: What external vendor partners does Winsupply rely on for M&A execution and why does consistency matter?
real_qa.r: Winsupply consistently hires Brixie Meyer for all quality of earnings (QV) analysis on every deal, large and small, and Seablee Shilton Dyers for legal work. Greg emphasizes that selecting external partners who 'think like you think and act like you act' ensures one unified vision when presenting to sellers. Having like-minded individuals across QV, legal, and internal vendor partners prevents personality conflicts and inconsistency. This consistency in external vendor partnerships is identified as key to deal success and effective execution.
real_qa.requete: Brixie Meyer Seablee Shilton Dyers M&A vendor partners

He joined Winsupply in 2010 to build the internal audit function and has progressively taken on roles in shared services, data management, and M&A, ultimately becoming Vice President of M&A where he handles all deal negotiations and runs M&A with a team of four people.
